title: Cashew Chicken
subtitle: tender chicken, crunchy toasted cashews and vegetables in a glossy honey-soy garlic sauce, over jasmine rice
imageAlt: Chicken pieces with cashews, broccoli and carrots in a glossy brown sauce over rice in a white bowl on a navy napkin
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Start the rice first. Stir-frying is fast, so have everything cut and the sauce mixed before you turn on the heat.

steps.title: Start the rice
steps.text: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear. Bring it to a boil with the water and a pinch of salt, cover and simmer on low 15 minutes, then rest 10 minutes off the heat with the lid on. Fluff with a fork.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Toss the chicken with 1 tbsp cornstarch and 1 tbsp soy sauce. Stir the sauce ingredients together: 3 tbsp soy sauce, the oyster sauce, honey, vinegar, 1 tbsp cornstarch, water and sesame oil.

steps.title: Toast the cashews
steps.text: Toast the cashews in a dry large skillet or wok over medium 3–4 minutes, shaking, until golden. Tip onto a plate.

steps.title: Cook the chicken
steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp of the oil over medium-high and cook the chicken in one layer 5–6 minutes, turning, until golden and 74°C (165°F). Move to a plate.

steps.title: Vegetables
steps.text: Add the remaining 1 tbsp oil, the broccoli, carrot and onion and stir-fry 4–5 minutes, until the broccoli is bright green and tender-crisp. Add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Sauce
steps.text: Stir the sauce, pour it in with the chicken and simmer 1–2 minutes, tossing, until thick and glossy. Toss in the cashews and serve over the rice.

fixIt.fix: Add a splash of water and toss; cornstarch sauces thicken fast.
Add them right at the end so they stay crunchy.
Cut the broccoli in small florets and the carrot thinly, or cover the pan for 1 minute.

saleTip: Bulk unsalted cashews at No Frills are cheaper than small bags; store extras in the freezer.
swap: Boneless thighs: same amount, cooked 6–7 minutes to 74°C (165°F).
leftovers: Keeps well for lunches; the cashews soften a little but still taste great.
doneness: Chicken pieces at 74°C (165°F) (Health Canada, poultry pieces). Reheat to 74°C (165°F).
source: Based on tested cashew chicken stir-fry methods (Canadian Living, The Woks of Life): cornstarch-marinated chicken, toasted cashews and a soy-oyster-honey sauce; dried chilies left out.
prepAhead: Cut the chicken and vegetables and mix the sauce up to 1 day ahead.
reheat: Covered in the microwave 2 minutes, stirring halfway, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Chicken and cashews in a honey-soy sauce; onion only.

stepNotes.1: Basic: sauce with soy, honey, vinegar, cornstarch and water.
stepNotes.4: Basic: onion and garlic only; stir-fry the onion 2–3 minutes.

fancy.note: Snow peas for crunch and toasted sesame seeds.

stepNotes.4: Fancy: add the snow peas with the broccoli.

addSteps.title: Sesame
addSteps.text: Scatter the sesame seeds over each bowl.

plating: Rice packed in a bowl and turned out.
Chicken and vegetables spooned beside it.

why.0-1: A cornstarch coating (velveting) keeps the chicken silky and helps the sauce cling.
why.2-0: Toasting the cashews deepens their flavour and crunch.
why.1-1: Oyster sauce adds the savoury takeout depth; it isn't fishy.

funFact: Cashew chicken in its saucy North American form was popularised in Springfield, Missouri, in the 1960s.

keeps.note: freeze without the rice; the cashews soften

pairs: fried rice instead of plain for a takeout night
